skill.name: data-structure-protocol
skill.description: Helps AI coding agents maintain a persistent DSP graph of code entities, imports, exports, and change impact.
skill.summary: Maintains a persistent codebase structure graph for AI-assisted navigation and refactoring.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static shell findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, command names, and code fence markers. The real issues are the unpinned curl download of dsp-cli.py and the workflow that runs that downloaded Python CLI against a project. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Ship dsp-cli.py with the skill, or pin it to a signed release and verify a published checksum before execution.
Declare network and external command behavior, and require user confirmation before downloading or running the CLI.
Document dry-run, backup, and confirmation steps before init, create, move, or remove operations change DSP metadata.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Remote CLI Download
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users or agents to download dsp-cli.py from a raw GitHub main branch URL, then run that Python CLI for project operations. This creates supply-chain risk because the downloaded script is not pinned or verified.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 86-92 direct retrieval from raw.githubusercontent.com and state that subsequent commands use python dsp-cli.py. The later examples show that CLI being executed for project operations.

semantic_findings.title: Risk Metadata Understates Command Behavior
semantic_findings.description: The front matter labels the skill risk as safe, but the body instructs network download and local CLI execution. Marketplace users may not receive clear warning before running the workflow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The risk declaration is visible on line 4, while lines 86-92 describe downloading and running external tooling. This is a clear mismatch in declared versus described behavior.

content.value_statement: Large codebases force agents to rediscover structure before each change. This skill guides a DSP graph that records entities, dependencies, exports, and change impact.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of a .dsp graph with object and function identifiers.
Defines when to create, update, move, or remove DSP entities.
Explains how to record imports, exports, and dependency reasons.
Provides a command reference for dsp-cli.py workflows.
Supports navigation through search, parents, children, paths, and recipients.
Frames impact analysis for replacing or changing dependencies.
limitations: Requires a separate Python CLI that is not included in the skill file.
Depends on accurate updates from the agent or user after code changes.
Does not analyze internals of external dependencies.
Adds .dsp files and source markers that teams must review.

use_cases.title: Plan a Refactor
use_cases.description: Locate affected entities and downstream recipients before changing a module or dependency.

use_cases.title: Maintain Structural Memory
use_cases.description: Keep a persistent graph of files, functions, imports, exports, and reasons across coding sessions.

use_cases.title: Review Architecture Changes
use_cases.description: Compare DSP updates with code diffs to verify that dependencies and public APIs stayed accurate.

prompt_templates.title: Create a DSP Map
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a project without DSP records.
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up DSP for this project. Identify root entry points, create the initial entity map, and summarize what files were recorded.

prompt_templates.title: Find Change Impact
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate navigation before modifying a feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DSP records to find every entity affected by changing the authentication flow. Include dependencies, recipients, and reasons.

prompt_templates.title: Update DSP After Changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate maintenance after a code edit.
prompt_templates.prompt: I changed public exports and imports in this feature. Update the DSP graph and explain each changed dependency reason.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Dependency Boundaries
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture review across a larger project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the DSP graph for risky dependency boundaries, orphaned entities, cycles, and modules with broad downstream impact.

output_examples.input: User asks where to change authentication validation.
output_examples.output: The skill reports the relevant authentication entities, their import reasons, and downstream modules that may need tests.

output_examples.input: User adds a new exported service function.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies the required DSP object, function, shared export, and dependency reason updates.

output_examples.input: User plans to replace a utility library.
output_examples.output: The skill lists modules that depend on the library and explains why each recipient imports it.

best_practices: Update DSP immediately after changes to files, imports, or public APIs.
Keep descriptions short and record clear reasons for every dependency.
Review .dsp changes together with the related code changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use DSP as a full documentation replacement.
Do not create entities for local variables or private helpers.
Do not download or run a CLI without verifying its source and checksum.

faq.question: What does this skill add to an AI coding workflow?
faq.answer: It gives the agent a persistent graph of code entities, dependencies, exports, and reasons for those relationships.

faq.question: Does it replace normal project documentation?
faq.answer: No. DSP is structural memory for agents, not full prose documentation for human readers.

faq.question: Does it require extra tooling?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow depends on dsp-cli.py and Python 3.10 or newer.

faq.question: Can it help before a refactor?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide impact analysis by showing import paths, recipients, and dependency reasons.

faq.question: How should external dependencies be represented?
faq.answer: They should be recorded as external entities without analyzing their internal source trees.

faq.question: What security caution applies?
faq.answer: Verify and pin any downloaded CLI before running it against a project repository.
